title: Load a level
description:
Write `parseLevel(text)` for Delve's level format. The text has lines separated by `\n` (ignore a trailing `\r`). Lines that start with `"# "` (hash and space) are comments, and blank lines are ignored; every other line is a map row.

Tiles: `#` wall, `.` floor, `+` door, `>` stairs. `@` is the player start and `g`, `k`, `t` are monster starts; all four have floor underneath.

Return a `Level` with the width, height, the tiles as a row-major string using only `#`, `.`, `+` and `>`, the player's start, and the monster spawns in reading order (top to bottom, left to right). If the level is invalid, return `std::nullopt`:

- no map rows at all,
- rows of different lengths,
- an unknown character,
- not exactly one `@`.

```
##### / #@.g# / #####   ->  width 5, height 3, tiles "######...######", player (1,1), spawns { g at (3,1) }
```
hints: `std::optional<T>` (from `<optional>`) holds either a `T` or nothing. `return value;` gives back a filled one and `return std::nullopt;` an empty one. A caller tests it with `if (result)` (or `result.has_value()`) and reads the value inside with `*result`.
Read the text line by line, skipping blanks and lines starting with `"# "`. The first map row sets the width; every later row must match it.
Use a `switch` on each character: the four tile characters go straight into `tiles`; `@` and the monster letters record a position and add `.` to `tiles`; anything else means the level is invalid.
The current row number is the number of map rows read so far (`height` before it is incremented).
